questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For my it was interesting to study political science in a country with such a different political history than what I'm used to and what counts for most of Western Europe. In that regards I wanted to go to one of the most different countries I could within the EU. Furthermore, it was important for me that there were some possibilities of exploring beautiful nature within a reachable distance of my exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to get information and there was a lot of meeting beforehand including guiding documents with information on the admission process and applying for courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day with social science, but I heard there was a whole introduction week at the humanities faculty, which I really wished I had the possibility too. Especially because it gave them a better social grounding right at the beggining.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy through Erasmus, but the possibilities was also better for us as we were four people. Outside of Erasmus it was very hard to find something for four people, so the Erasmus was crucial for us in finding an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was very nice to have your own apartment. Both in terms of privacy and the possibility to invite new friends over.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process itself was easy, but since I had some obligatory courses from my home university I had to replace, I had problems when I arrived, because some courses I was counting on taking wasn't offered or was exclusively for non-Erasmus students. This information lacked and made my process too difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We received information beforehand. Then the registration opened at different timeslots for different faculties with a first-come-first-served process, but if you didn't get into a courses you wanted to could register for a waiting list and the professors were very flexible in terms of allowing students not on the official lists to participate in the first class. There was also a flexible period in the beginning where you could register for more courses than you needed to check them out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom meeting, helping manuals and very fast responding Erasmus coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have some back-up courses in case your plan A doesn't work

All of my courses, except one, was on master level, but the generel level of the courses was surprisingly low, although I had two very good courses. My only bachelor course was on a high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of focus on oral participation in the classes and an overall grade reflecting not only the exam but the performance throughout the whole semester. This differed a lot from what I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ASZTV0068: Bouldering
JEB026: European Economic Integration
JPM805: Democracy - Current Challenges and Innovations
JSM777: EU Comparative Politics:Tensions in Representative Democracy
JTM254: Promoting democracy abroad: the US and the EU in third countries
JTM382: EU Institutions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Promoting democracy abroad: the US and the EU in third countries. The teacher is one of the best I have come across. The discussions in class was very good and interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up spending a lot of money on transport going back and forth because I didn't want to fly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport within the Czech Republic was very inexpensive. I had thought my rent would be cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sport opportunities, everyone could sign up for one sports-course. There were some activities in the beginning for the faculty. There wasn't a lot of information about other clubs or "local" life on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a sports course. I met a lot of very nice Czech students there!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to the close other big  European cities (Berlin, Budapest, Wein). I also went to Bohemian Switzerland, where Narnia was filmed and to Špindlerův Mlýn to go skiing- both things was very fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have been in Prague many times before, so it was very easy. I also lived with three people that i knew from home, which also made it more easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the events (I didn't, and i regretted it) and don't be afraid to just talk to people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find any cultural differences particularly challenging. Some people didn't speak english, but that is fair enough.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The use of parks. the Czech people loves nature, why they also use the parks a lot! You can also swim in some parts of the river and in some lakes. There were also a lot of concerts and events that were easy to find!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Worth paying for private life
2. Go into nature and use the cheap culture options in the city
3. Go to the events in the beginning - but you don't need to go party

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get the goout app!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all my friends!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling confident in the social aspect of exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
